sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 covers the northern edge of downtown Madison at 50 feet to an inch, with north towards the upper right. Ridgedale Avenue crosses the top of the sheet, Park Avenue runs down its west side of block 67 and continues south as Main Street, and Cook Avenue bounds the block on the east. Oak runs between Park Avenue and Cook Avenue across the middle of the sheet. The block between Ridgedale Avenue and Oak holds a few dwellings, a storage building, a shed and several automobile buildings, including an auto repair shop and a garage with a stone filling station, mostly on the Cook Avenue side. Along the west side of Main Street below Oak are a cabinet shop and upholstering works, a tailor, an auto supplies and upholstering shop, and a row of small stores, followed by the Y.M.C.A. building with its gymnasium and swimming pool, tenements, a fruit store, a jeweler and grocery stores. The Public Library stands in the triangle between Main Street and the D.L.&W. railroad near the bottom, beside Green Village Road. The railroad, with its double track, crosses the sheet from top to bottom and passes Madison Avenue and Green Village Road on concrete bridges. Kings Road runs down the left side beyond the railroad. A small park lies between Madison Avenue and Park Avenue, and the blocks on the east side of Cook Avenue and the left of Kings Road are blank, left to neighbouring sheets. Water pipes, hydrants and street widths are marked throughout.
notes: Oak is today Community Place.
The printed Park Avenue continues south as Main Street; the modern Park Avenue / Main Street node lies about 40 m south of Oak and no junction is drawn there.
Madison Avenue / Kings Road / Main Street at the upper left is not used for control; the sheet draws it as a bridge crossing, not a clear junction.
Fitted scale is 7.96 px/ft against 8.04 expected for 50 ft to an inch.
50 ft (scale of feet). Downtown: Ridgedale Av, Green Village Rd, Main St, Cook Av, Kings Rd, railroad.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 shows the commercial centre of Madison at 50 feet to an inch, with the compass arrow pointing towards the upper right. Main Street runs down the middle of the sheet and Waverly Place, a wide open street along the north side of the Main Street shops, crosses it from the railroad to Central Avenue. The block north of Waverly Place, block 87 and block 88 beyond Main Street, holds the post office, a bank, drug and notions stores, a printing office, markets, a telephone exchange with a lodge room, a garage and a hardware and fertilizer warehouse. Central Avenue bounds block 88 on the south and meets Cook Avenue at the right edge. South of Central Avenue and east of Main Street, block 99 contains a bank, restaurant, laundry, bakery, Red Cross rooms, the police station, a furniture and undertaking store, and dwellings. West of Main Street, between Waverly Place, Lincoln Place and Prospect, are the Madison House, the American House, a livery and carriage works, garages, the American Seed Tape Company, and rows of small shops and dwellings. Piersons Alley crosses block 98. The double-track D.L.&W. railroad runs down the left side with the passenger depot, express building and covered platforms drawn in blue and brown. Kings Road lies along the left edge beyond the railroad and Greenwood Avenue crosses the bottom right. The area at the left is largely open ground with only the compass rose and block number 15.
notes: The printed Cook Avenue north of Central Avenue and Elmer south of it are offset on the sheet; OpenStreetMap has one node, Central Avenue / Cook Avenue / Elmer Street.
The compass arrow points about 29 degrees right of vertical; the fit gives true north at about 39 degrees, sheet 2's arrow differs from this one by about 10 degrees in the same sense.
Lincoln Place / Prospect Street and Kings Road / Prospect Street fall just off the bottom edge and were not used.
50 ft (scale of feet). Downtown: Main St, Waverly Pl, Central Av, Lincoln Pl, Kings Rd, Greenwood Av, Prospect St, Cook Av, Elmer St; D.L.&W. passenger depot.

sheet-4-1.description: Sheet 4, part 1, shows the north-western edge of Madison at 100 feet to an inch, drawn with north towards the upper right. On the left is a small residential district of detached frame dwellings between Morris Place and Fairwood Road, laid out in blocks 24, 26, 27, 28, 29 and 30 along Ferndale, Forest, Woodside and Fairwood Roads. Glendale Road runs in a curve from Forest Road to Woodside Road and continues as a straight street between blocks 29 and 30, ending at the lower Fairwood Road. Most houses are of frame construction, many of them stuccoed, with automobile garages and a few poultry houses behind them, and Danforth Road and Fairwood Road carry water pipes. A brick dwelling stands at the left in block 27. The D.L.&W. railroad runs down the middle of the sheet in a double-track curve with the St. Ry right of way beside it. To the east are the large estates of H. H. Binnse, with a pond, Lenox Rose and R. B. Holmes, whose greenhouses stand near the bottom, along the diagonal of Park Avenue; to the west block 31 is the Estate of J. M. Youngs, marked all buildings vacant. West Street, Center Street, Holmes Street, Binnse Street and North Street meet at the bottom. An inset at the lower right, bounded by a heavy line and carrying its own compass, continues the map east of Park Avenue; it is a separate part.
notes: Printed Danforth R'd, Ferndale R'd and the other R'd names are Road; the printed Morris Pl. is Morris Place.
Holmes, Binnse Street and Center Street are not in OpenStreetMap.
Glendale Road / Woodside Road (two nodes 3 m apart) was rejected at 9 m; the curved Glendale Road does not fit the modern node.
The compass arrow at the lower right points about 55 degrees right of vertical, in agreement with the fitted rotation of 52.7 degrees.

100 ft. North-west district: Ferndale, Forest, Fairwood, Glendale, Woodside Rds, Morris Pl, Danforth Rd, Park Av, railroad. Two parts: part 1 main; part 2 heavy-lined inset at lower right (Danforth Rd / Park Av, H. H. Binnse), not placed.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset at lower right: Park Avenue and Danforth Road, H. H. Binnse property (only one junction (Danforth Road / Park Avenue), at the image edge; needs step 6b: carried points from sheet 5 or parcel corners).

sheet-5-1.description: Sheet 5, part 1, is the north-eastern fringe of Madison, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. Most of it is open land on the borough boundary: large estate lots (blocks 34 and 35) held by J. H. Sussman and J. S. Gilbertson, with a few farm buildings, a brook that rises near the top right and runs down to North Street through a long, thin pond, and a dash-dot line marking the boundary with the Borough of Florham Park across the upper half. Parr Avenue runs down the left edge. In the lower left, North Street crosses the sheet on a diagonal from Parr Avenue towards the lower right, with Holmes Street and Center Street entering it from the south and East Street near the right. Block 40 along the north side of North Street is divided into narrow lots running back from the street, each with a frame dwelling or two, sheds, poultry houses and a long glasshouse, numbered from 4 to 78. South of North Street the blocks (7 at the left) are left blank for sheet 7, and block 5 appears at the lower right. A rectangular inset at the upper right, bounded by a heavy line and showing North Street, Myrtle Avenue and Burnett Road, is a separate part.
notes: The street at the left edge is lettered Parr Av. on this sheet but Park Av. on sheet 4; it is today Park Avenue.
Center Street and Holmes Street are not in OpenStreetMap.
The part is placed by two points only, East Street / North Street and Park Avenue / North Street (the second hand-picked at the left edge), so scale and rotation are rough; the fit gives 4.07 px/ft.
The compass arrow near the upper right edge points about 21 degrees right of vertical; the fit gives about 32 degrees.

100 ft (bar "Scale 100 Ft. to One Inch"). Two parts: part 1 North St strip with Parr (Park) Av, Center, East and Holmes Sts; part 2 inset at top right with North St, Myrtle Av and Burnett (Burnet) Rd. Both two-point helmerts.

sheet-5-2.description: Sheet 5, part 2, is a rectangular inset at the top right of the sheet, enclosed by a heavy line, at the same scale of 100 feet to an inch. It shows a strip of North Street running across the bottom of the inset with Myrtle Avenue entering it from the south at the left and Burnett Road, a street along the borough line, rising towards the upper right from the right-hand end. The area above North Street is open land in blocks 5 and 35, crossed by thin lot lines, with a handful of dwellings, sheds and farm buildings strung out along Burnett Road and a dash-dot line for the boundary of the Borough of Florham Park in the top corner. Water pipes of 4 inches run along North Street and Burnett Road with street widths of 50 feet marked, and block number 8 stands on the south side of North Street. The street grid is drawn at a slightly different angle from the main part of the sheet, which is why it is shown as a separate inset.
notes: Burnett Road is today Burnet Road in OpenStreetMap.

The part is placed by two points only, North Street / Myrtle Avenue (hand-picked, Myrtle Avenue is cut by the inset border) and North Street / Burnet Road, so it is a helmert with a fitted scale of 4.00 px/ft.

100 ft (bar "Scale 100 Ft. to One Inch"). Two parts: part 1 North St strip with Parr (Park) Av, Center, East and Holmes Sts; part 2 inset at top right with North St, Myrtle Av and Burnett (Burnet) Rd. Both two-point helmerts.

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 covers the north-western approach to downtown Madison at 100 feet to an inch, with north towards the upper right. Madison Avenue runs down the left side from Elm Street and Lancaster Road to the bottom of the sheet, while Park Avenue forms the right side, narrowing as it runs south to Ridgedale Avenue. Between them a double-track railroad, the right of way of the Morris County Traction Company, runs from top to bottom beside the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western line, and block 55 west of it is mostly open land with scattered frame dwellings on deep lots. In the upper middle, West Street and Elm Street meet at a wedge where block 42 is cut up by two short streets named Center. East of the tracks, the district between Holmes, Binnse and Park Avenue is a small neighbourhood of frame dwellings in blocks 44 and 45, with poultry houses and sheds. Old St. Vincent's School, marked as not in use, stands on Park Avenue, and a diagonal street cuts through the block north of East Park Street. At the bottom the C. C. Force and Son machine shop, with a watchman, power, heat and fuel notes, faces Park Avenue, and a rest pavilion is drawn in blue near the foot of Madison Avenue. South Street and North Street leave Park Avenue at the top right.
notes: Holmes, Binnse and Center are not in OpenStreetMap; East Park Street is also absent.
The compass arrow at the upper left points about 25 degrees right of vertical; the fit gives about 39 degrees.
Park Avenue and Ridgedale Avenue meet at the bottom edge, where sheet 2 continues.
100 ft. Madison Av, Park Av, Elm, West, Center, Holmes, Binnse, North and South Sts, Lancaster Rd.

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7 shows the district east of downtown Madison at 100 feet to an inch, drawn with north towards the upper right. North Street crosses the top of the sheet and South Street runs parallel below it, enclosing blocks 46 and 47, divided by Center, a street that runs down from North Street beside a brook; the blocks are divided into narrow lots running back from the street, each with a frame dwelling and sheds, poultry houses or a small shop. Block 48 at the upper right stands between East Street, North Street and the edge of the sheet beside a proposed road, with dwellings, storage buildings and a bake oven. Park Avenue runs down the left side, East Street runs diagonally down the middle and Myrtle Avenue runs down the right, with Howard Street and E. Park joining them. The middle of the sheet is open farmland in blocks 50 and 56, crossed by a brook that runs south across Elm Street and E. Park and joins a second small stream. Dwellings stand along the west side of Park Avenue and the east side of Myrtle Avenue, and The Ridgedale Inn and an ice house stand on Ridgedale Avenue, which crosses the bottom of the sheet from Park Avenue to the right edge. Walnut Street and Cook Avenue enter Ridgedale Avenue from the south, where sheet 2 begins.
notes: Howard Street was left out of the fit: its junctions with East Street and Myrtle Avenue were 5.9 m and 4.8 m off, against about 2 m for the rest, so the modern line is probably displaced from the drawn one.
Center, E. Park and Proposed Road are not in OpenStreetMap.
The compass arrow near the middle points almost straight down the sheet, while the fit gives true north about 17 degrees right of vertical.
100 ft. North, South, East, Center Sts, Myrtle Av, Park Av, Ridgedale Av; Howard St left out (modern line about 5 m off).

sheet-8-1.description: Sheet 8 shows the northern edge of Madison borough, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. The main drawing lies between North Street at the top, Myrtle Avenue down the left edge and Burnett Road, which runs from the top edge diagonally down the middle to meet Ridgedale Avenue. Ridgedale Avenue crosses the lower part of the sheet from the lower left to the right edge, with Fairview Avenue joining it near a row of small dwellings on its north side. Howard Street and a street lettered Prosposed Street are laid out between Myrtle Avenue and Burnett Road, but only the outlines of the blocks are drawn there, and most of the sheet is open land in large numbered blocks (36, 49, 51, 57). A few frame dwellings stand on North Street, Myrtle Avenue and Ridgedale Avenue, and a row of dwellings with long narrow lots lines the north side of Ridgedale Avenue east of Burnett Road. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches are drawn along the streets. A borough line of Florham Park crosses the upper right. The lower right corner, inside a heavy line, is a separate block configured as part 2.
notes: The street lettered Prosposed Street is printed with that spelling and does not exist today.
Burnett Road is Burnet Road in OpenStreetMap; North is North Street.
Only four street junctions were measured, so the fit is weakly controlled.

100 ft. Two parts: part 1 North St, Myrtle Av, Burnett Rd, Howard St, "Prosposed St." (printed so), Ridgedale Av; part 2 heavy-lined block at lower right on Ridgedale Av at Central Av (Twombly greenhouses), anchored on one junction.

sheet-8-2.description: This block fills the lower right corner of sheet 8, inside a heavy line, at 100 feet to an inch. It shows Ridgedale Avenue running from the lower left towards the upper right, with Central Avenue leaving it to the south near the right edge, and a borough line of Florham Park crossing the upper part. The Estate of H. McK. Twombly, with C. H. Totty as lessee, occupies a range of long greenhouses and a potting house at the top. Most of the block, numbered 36, is open land. A compass and the printed sheet numbers 8 and 12 stand beside the heavy line. The block is drawn at a different place from the main part of the sheet and continues on sheet 12.
notes: Placed from the single Central Avenue / Ridgedale Avenue junction with the sheet scale and an assumed rotation; low confidence.
The block is not the continuation of the main part of sheet 8; it overlaps the area on the left of sheet 12.

100 ft. Two parts: part 1 North St, Myrtle Av, Burnett Rd, Howard St, "Prosposed St." (printed so), Ridgedale Av; part 2 heavy-lined block at lower right on Ridgedale Av at Central Av (Twombly greenhouses), anchored on one junction.

sheet-9.description: Sheet 9 covers the centre-north of Madison, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. Ridgedale Avenue crosses the top edge, Cook Avenue runs down the left side and Central Avenue crosses the sheet on a diagonal from the lower left to the right edge. Walnut Street runs south from Ridgedale Avenue to Central Avenue, and Chapel, Brittin and Locust Streets run south from Central Avenue, with Howell Street between Brittin and Locust. Greenwood Avenue closes the sheet at the bottom, where Elmer Street also meets it. The upper blocks are mostly open land (blocks 70 and 71) with scattered dwellings and a hollow tile stuccoed building on Ridgedale Avenue, while the Central Avenue Public School stands in the middle. Dwellings line Cook Avenue, which carries a Baptist church and, at its foot, a fire department building near Central Avenue. A baseball park fills the block between Chapel and Brittin Streets. Greenhouses appear at the right edge. Water mains and hydrants are marked along the streets, and a stretch of Grove Street leaves Greenwood Avenue to the south.
notes: Oak Street is lettered at the left edge as a dashed water-main label near Cook Avenue.
Thirteen junctions were detected automatically.
100 ft. Ridgedale Av, Cook Av, Walnut, Central Av, Chapel, Elmer, Brittin, Howell, Greenwood Av, Locust, Grove St.

sheet-10.description: Sheet 10 covers a residential district east of downtown Madison, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. It is bounded by Greenwood Avenue along the top, Main Street down the left side, Grove Street on the right and Rosedale Avenue, which crosses the lower part of the sheet on a diagonal. Prospect Street, Elmer Street and Chapel Street meet Greenwood Avenue at the top edge; Alexander and Highland Avenue cross the middle, Brittin runs between Greenwood Avenue and Highland Avenue, and Cross Street and Oak Street meet Rosedale Avenue at the lower left. The blocks along Greenwood Avenue, Alexander and Grove are lined with frame dwellings on narrow lots, many with automobile garages behind them, and several houses are marked as stuccoed. The large block between Main Street and Brittin holds the Main Street Public School and the American Seed Tape Company with its storage building, and the Presbyterian Church of Madison faces Main Street lower down. The Rose City Inn stands on Main Street near Cross Street. The blocks east of Brittin and south of Highland Avenue are only partly built up, with poultry houses and open lots, and the area below Rosedale Avenue is left blank for sheet 17. Water pipes and their sizes are drawn along the streets, with hydrants and street widths noted. Block numbers 117 to 124 are printed with the older numbers in brackets, and a borough line runs along the right edge.
notes: Main Street Public School and the American Seed Tape Company share the block between Main and Brittin.
Presbyterian Church of Madison and the Rose City Inn face Main Street.
100 ft. Greenwood Av, Main, Alexander, Brittin, Grove, Highland Av, Rosedale Av (pilot). North about +44 deg (upper right).

sheet-11.description: Sheet 11 lies north-east of the centre of Madison, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. Ridgedale Avenue curves down the left side, Fairview Avenue crosses the upper part from the left edge to the upper right, Central Avenue runs south from Fairview Avenue through the middle, and Greenwood Avenue runs down the right side. Burnett Road meets Ridgedale Avenue near the left edge. The sheet is largely greenhouses and open land: W. H. Barton and T. W. Stemmler greenhouses stand between Ridgedale and Central Avenues, and David Shannon greenhouses near the bottom. Dwellings are scattered along Fairview and Central Avenues, with narrow lots between Central and Greenwood Avenues (block 104). The upper left is blank, being part of block 12 on the neighbouring sheet. Water pipes and hydrants are drawn along the streets, and the borough line and Greenwood Avenue pass the right edge. A compass stands near the top.
notes: Burnett Road is Burnet Road in OpenStreetMap.

The drawn junction of Fairview Avenue and Greenwood Avenue at the top right lies about 45 m from where sheet 12 places it, and modern Greenwood Avenue and Fairview Avenue are realigned there; it was not used.
Only three junctions were used (all in the western half), so the fit is weakly controlled.
100 ft. Ridgedale, Fairview, Central and Greenwood Avs, Burnett Rd; exact three-point fit (Greenwood/Fairview realigned).

sheet-12.description: Sheet 12 shows the north-eastern fringe of Madison and the adjoining Borough of Florham Park, drawn at 200 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. Ridgedale Avenue runs down the left edge. Central Avenue leaves it near the upper left and runs south-east to Fairview Avenue, which crosses the lower left. Rosedale Avenue runs from the upper left diagonally to the centre, where Greenwood Avenue, Fairview Avenue and Rosedale Avenue meet, and Rosedale Avenue continues to the lower right. East Madison Avenue joins Greenwood Avenue from the east. Greenwood Avenue runs south to the bottom edge. Greenhouses stand at the upper left and top centre, including Chas. Totty and C. P. Dudly, and the Maple Hill Health Resort stands near Central Avenue. Most of the sheet is open land in large numbered blocks (37, 38, 59, 60, 61, 121, 122, 124). Borough lines of Florham Park cross the upper half and a compass stands at the top right.
notes: Printed Rosedale Avenue; its modern continuation is also Rosedale Avenue near the junction with Greenwood Avenue.
Only three junctions, all at the left edge, control the fit; the east side is extrapolated and low confidence.
The Fairview / Greenwood junction was not used: it falls about 45 m from where sheet 11 places the same junction.
200 ft. Ridgedale, Central, Fairview, Rosedale, Greenwood and East Madison Avs towards Florham Park; exact three-point fit, all control at the left edge.

sheet-13.description: Sheet 13 covers the south-western part of Madison near the Chatham township line, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. Glenwood Road runs along the top and Woodland Road crosses the sheet, with Lathrop Avenue parallel to it below. Loantaka Way and Gibbons Place run down the left edge and Orchard Street joins Woodland Road and Lathrop Avenue in the middle. Green Village Road forms the right side, and Drew Place starts at the lower right. A narrow strip of dwellings lines Woodland Road and Lathrop Avenue with their rear sheds and poultry houses, while the large blocks above and below (63, 74, 76, 77) are mostly open, with the estates of Arthur Decker and Peter Stryker at upper left and Mrs. White and Hebbie Naughton Est. at lower right. Greenhouses stand on Gibbons Place. The Township of Chatham borough line crosses the bottom of the sheet. Water mains and hydrants are lettered along the streets and a compass stands lower centre.
notes: Glenwood Road has no match in the OpenStreetMap extract under that name.
Six junctions were detected automatically with an RMSE of 0.7 m.
100 ft. Glenwood Rd, Loantaka Way, Woodland Rd, Lathrop Av, Gibbons Pl, Green Village Rd, Prospect Pl.

sheet-14.description: Sheet 14 lies in the south-west of Madison, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. Green Village Road runs along the top from the left to the upper right, and Glenwood Road meets it from above. Woodland Road runs south through the middle and Crescent Road curves from Green Village Road down to Hillside Avenue on the right. Hillcrest Road curves down the left side to Midwood Terrace, and Highview Terrace and Drew Place lie at the left edge with a stub of Lathrop Avenue at the top left. Green Avenue crosses the lower part and Prospect crosses at the bottom, where Webb Avenue and Maple Avenue meet Hillside Avenue to the right. The blocks are large and mostly open, with scattered frame dwellings (R. Eagles, Mrs. Gordon, W. A. Robbins, Harrison, Condit and Walter H. Condit among the names), blocks 64, 79, 82, 83, 94 and 95. Green Hill Road enters at the right edge. Water mains and hydrants are lettered along the streets.
notes: Green Village Road was left out of the fit: its junctions carried residuals of 4 to 6 m (RMSE 3.6 m with it, 1.2 m without).
Midwood Terrace and Highview Terrace are lettered on the sheet; Hillcrest Road is the modern name of the road beneath Midwood Terrace.
100 ft. Green Village Rd, Crescent Rd, Hillside Av, Green Av, Midwood and Highview Ters, Prospect St; Green Village Road left out of the control (displaced).

sheet-15.description: Sheet 15 covers a residential district south of the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad in Madison, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. The railroad and its concrete bridges cross the top of the sheet, with Kings Road, Waverly Place and Lincoln Place drawn between the tracks and the first blocks. Green Village Road runs diagonally down the left side, Prospect Street forms the right edge and Hillside Avenue the bottom. Wilmer and Vinton Road cross the middle, and Green Avenue and Maple Avenue run down the centre and right. The large block between Kings Road, Green Village Road and Wilmer holds St. Vincent's R.C. Church with its rectory and parochial school, the Presbyterian Church of Madison with Webb Memorial Chapel, and the Green Avenue Public School. The Eagle Club House stands at the top of the same block. Joseph M. Smith's planning mill and mill work, with storage buildings, occupies the upper right corner beside Prospect Street. Lower down are large dwellings on spacious lots (W. H. Seward, E. D. Conklin, E. A. Rosenfeld, F. G. Allsbrook, Mrs. Anderson, H. L. Serviss, W. E. Schenck) and a long range of greenhouses in block 84. Narrow frame dwellings line Green Avenue and Maple Avenue. Block numbers 65, 66, 84, 85, 86, 96 and 97 are printed with the older numbers in brackets, and water pipes, hydrants and street widths are marked along the streets.
notes: Kings Road, Lincoln Place and Waverly Place are drawn along the railroad cut and do not follow the modern OpenStreetMap lines, so they were left out of the control points.
Printed Wilmer is Wilmer Street today.
Prospect is Prospect Street today; Pomeroy Av. at the right edge is Pomeroy Road in OpenStreetMap.
The surrounding sheets are numbered 2, 3, 14, 16, 19, 21 and 22 at the margins.
Keep Street at the right edge is hard to read on the scan (medium confidence).
100 ft. Residential district south of the railroad: Kings Rd, Green Village Rd, Wilmer, Vinton Rd, Hillside Av, Waverly Pl, Lincoln Pl, Belmont Av, Pomeroy Av, Keep St; St. Vincent's church.

sheet-16.description: Sheet 16 covers the Madison railroad district south and east of the downtown, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. Main Street forms the top edge, Prospect Street the left edge, Cross Street the upper right and Pomeroy Avenue the bottom. Keep Street and Belmont Avenue run across the lower part, and Kings Road passes diagonally from Prospect Street across the sheet to Cross Street. The Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad crosses in a broad band of tracks, with sidings and the D. L. and W. R. R. freight depot in block 115. North of the tracks lie Green and Pierson's coal and lumber yard with its storage and sheds, a garage on Main Street, and a large unbuilt cemetery tract (block 116) crossed by a brook near Cross Street. South of the tracks the Morris Coal and Lumber Company and the Joseph M. Smith coal and lumber works occupy the blocks along Prospect Street, with a lumber shed and potting houses nearby. Blocks 112 and 113 between Keep Street and Pomeroy Avenue hold small dwellings and greenhouses on narrow lots. The right half below the tracks, blocks 114 and 134, is largely vacant. Block numbers carry older numbers in brackets, and water pipes and street widths are marked.
notes: Printed Main, Prospect, Cross and Keep are Main Street, Prospect Street, Cross Street and Keep Street today.
Potwin Avenue (right edge) is not in the OpenStreetMap extract; Pomeroy Avenue is Pomeroy Road today.
Kings Road is drawn as a diagonal beside the railroad; its junction with Prospect Street was used with caution.
Cross Street junctions were used here but proved displaced against sheet 17 (see sheet 17 notes).
100 ft. Railroad district: Main, Prospect, Cross, Pomeroy Av, Keep, Belmont Av, Kings Rd, Potwin Av, Lincoln Pl, Rosedale Av; coal and lumber yards.

sheet-17.description: Sheet 17 covers the south-eastern edge of Madison along Main Street, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. Rosedale Avenue enters at the left edge and runs along a diagonal, Cross Street forms the left side of the lower part, and Main Street crosses the sheet from left to right at about two thirds of the height. Station Road leaves Main Street towards the upper right, and Samson Avenue, Lloyd Road and Burns Street run south of Main Street, with Kings Road along the bottom edge. Oak Avenue and Cottage Place are short cross streets near the left. A winding brook flows from the top of the sheet down to Main Street. The Madison Municipal Electric Light and Pumping Station, with its pond and a note that a man is always on duty, stands at the upper right. North of Main Street the sheet is mostly open land in blocks 131, 132 and 137, with a few farm buildings and poultry houses scattered along Main Street. South of Main Street the blocks 130, 135 and 136 are built up with frame dwellings, some with automobile garages, and a green house stands in block 136. An abandoned railroad right of way crosses block 135 diagonally. A borough line is drawn along the top edge and a dotted line down the right edge.
notes: Oak Avenue is Dean Street in OpenStreetMap; Burns is Bruns Street today.
Cross Street is drawn bending more than the modern line; its junctions fell 4 to 8 m from a fit to the Main Street and Kings Road junctions and were left out of the control points.
Lloyd Road is not in the OpenStreetMap extract.
An abandoned railroad right of way crosses block 135.

100 ft. South-east Main St: Rosedale Av, Station Rd, Samson Av, Cottage Pl, Cross, Burns (Bruns St), Kings Rd; municipal electric light and pumping station. Cross Street left out of the control (junctions 4.5 to 7.8 m off).

sheet-18.description: Sheet 18 shows the southeastern edge of Madison along Main Street towards the Chatham boundary, at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. Main Street crosses the lower third of the sheet from left to right; below it Seaman, Union Avenue and Division Avenue run down to Kings Road, which crosses the bottom of the sheet. Brooklake Road runs up the right edge along the borough line, beyond which is the Borough of Chatham. A strip marked Abandoned R.R. Right of Way crosses the blocks between Main Street and Kings Road on a diagonal, the line of an old railroad bed. The north side of Main Street is divided into long, narrow lots running back to the borough line, with dwellings near the street and poultry houses and sheds behind; the land above them, block 148 and the area around a pond at the upper left, is open and undeveloped, with a small group of farm buildings near Brooklake Road. Block 143 lies north of Main Street at the left. South of Main Street, blocks 136, 141, 142 and 147 hold scattered frame dwellings, poultry houses and automobile sheds. Water pipes run along Main Street, Kings Road and Division Avenue with hydrants marked, and the street widths of Union Avenue and Division Avenue are noted. Most of the upper two thirds of the sheet is empty farmland, which leaves few drawn street junctions; all control lies along the bottom band of the sheet.
notes: Abandoned railroad right of way crosses between Main Street and Kings Road.
Brooklake Road forms the borough line with Chatham.
100 ft. Main St from Seaman to Division Av/Brooklake Rd, Kings Rd, Union Av; abandoned railroad right of way; upper two thirds open farmland. North about -39 deg (upper left).

sheet-19.description: Sheet 19 covers an outlying residential and estate district south-west of Madison, drawn at 200 feet to an inch with north towards the right. Green Village Road runs across the top and Shunpike Road down the left edge along the Chatham township line. Garfield Avenue runs from Green Village Road south through the middle to Woodland Road, Green Avenue crosses the upper middle, and Hillcrest Road, drawn with a green macadam line, curves down the upper right to meet Prospect Street. Midwood Terrace and Woodland Road run south-east from there and Webb Avenue and Pomeroy Avenue are drawn at the lower right. The land is divided into large numbered blocks (80, 89 to 93, 105 to 111) held by private estates, among them Edward Behr, A. P. Smith, Chas. Work, the estate of A. G. Evans, E. F. Frenz, Mrs. John H. Ross, A. R. Palmer, E. S. Wilsey, Bertha Schundler, Wm. A. Starrett, Wm. O. Ludlow, Spencer S. Marsh and the estate of Jas. R. Webb. Several estates carry rows of greenhouses and a water works stands beside Midwood. Dwellings are small and scattered; the Township of Chatham at the left is only lightly built. Water pipes and dwellings are marked, and the sheet joins numbers 13, 14, 15, 16, 20 and 21 at its margins.
notes: Printed Prospect is Prospect Street today; Pomeroy Avenue is Pomeroy Road.
Webb Avenue and Drew Place are not in the OpenStreetMap extract.
Shunpike Road junctions fell 5 to 6 m from the fit and were left out of the control points.
Drawn at 200 feet to an inch; the fit gives 2.01 pixels per foot.
Woodland Road and Midwood Terrace junction sits about 4 m from its modern node.
200 ft. South-west estates: Green Village Rd, Shunpike Rd, Garfield Av, Hillcrest Rd, Woodland Rd, Webb Av, Pomeroy Av.

sheet-20.description: Sheet 20 covers a thinly built district south of Madison at the borough boundary, drawn at 200 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. Garfield Avenue enters at the top left and joins Woodland Road, which curves south-east down the middle of the sheet. Pomeroy Avenue and Potwin Avenue run along the top, Samson Avenue crosses the upper middle and Noe Avenue crosses the lower middle from the Chatham boundary on the left. Watchung Avenue and Shunpike Road run down the left edge and Kings Road down the right edge, with Union Avenue and Division Avenue at the lower right. The Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad runs in a band of parallel tracks from top right to bottom centre. Most of the sheet is held in large blocks (126, 127, 133, 134, 139, 144) belonging to estates, among them the estate of H. D. Hutchins, W. F. Harris (admittance refused to the grounds), the estate of Henry Hentz and Duckham, Pierson and Co. florists, whose rows of greenhouses fill the lower left. Noe-Ruzicka and Brant-Noe greenhouses stand at the left. Dwellings are widely scattered, with a small cluster near Union Avenue. A private road runs across the lower part, and a note at the bottom edge reads 'See Map of Chatham'. A borough line follows the left and bottom edges.
notes: Georeferenced from three street junctions only (Pomeroy Road / Samson Avenue, Kings Road / Union Avenue, Kings Road / Division Avenue); low confidence.
Woodland Road junctions did not fit with the others (5 to 20 m) and were left out.
Pomeroy Avenue is Pomeroy Road in OpenStreetMap; Potwin Avenue is not in the extract.
Burns Street is Bruns Street today.
Abandoned Street is drawn but no longer exists.

200 ft. Estates and greenhouses at the Chatham line: Garfield, Pomeroy, Potwin, Samson, Noe, Watchung, Union, Division Avs, Woodland, Shunpike and Kings Rds. Woodland Road left out of the control (6 to 12 m off).

sheet-21.description: Sheet 21 covers a western fringe of Madison, drawn at 200 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. Madison Avenue enters at the top left, bends at Loantaka Way and runs east to Lancaster Road at the right edge. Loantaka Way runs south down the left-centre of the sheet to Glenwood Road at the bottom, where Woodland Road comes in at the lower left and Green Village Road at the lower right. Morris Place, drawn with a green macadam line, runs along the top right, and Vinal Place and Lancaster Road cross the upper right. The upper right has small suburban lots in blocks 4, 22 and 41 along Morris Place and Madison Avenue (J. Corrett, Frank McEwan, A. L. Page, Wm. Davies, A. E. McAlpin, Sidell Tilghman). Along Loantaka Way the sheet is held by large estates, notably Mrs. Geraldine R. Dodge, whose house, greenhouse and farm buildings stand left of the way, and Geo. W. Downs, Henry Feuchtwanger, W. S. Sterns, J. C. Humbert and Geo. Wilder on the right. The Township of Chatham lies along the left edge behind a borough line. Blocks 21, 39, 40, 52 and 53 are mostly open land. A circular drive of the seminary grounds shows at the lower right edge.
notes: Georeferenced from a single hand-picked junction (Madison Avenue / Vinal Place) at the configured scale and a north direction of -9 degrees; low confidence.
Madison Avenue west of Loantaka Way is drawn off the modern OpenStreetMap line and was not used.
Lancaster Road / Madison Avenue was detected 13 m from the fit and left out.
Glenwood Road is not in the OpenStreetMap extract.

200 ft. Loantaka Way estates (Mrs. Geraldine R. Dodge), Madison Av, Morris Pl, Vinal Pl, Lancaster Rd, Glenwood Rd. Placed from two junctions on Madison Av only: Glenwood Rd is not the modern Woodland Road (a trial gave 12 m RMSE), Madison Av / Loantaka Way has moved.

sheet-22.description: Sheet 22 covers the grounds of the Drew Theological Seminary and the adjoining blocks along Madison Avenue, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. Lancaster Road runs along the top edge, Madison Avenue down the right edge, and Green Village Road across the bottom left, with Academy Road making a loop and then running to Green Village Road at the left. The seminary buildings stand in the middle in a campus laid out with underground water mains: Samuel W. Bowne Hall with its kitchen and dining hall, the Gymnasium with swimming pool, the Administration Building, Mead Hall with mission class rooms and offices, Cornell Memorial Library, Hoyt Bowne Building, Asbury Hall, Embury Hall with the heating plant, and the President's dwelling. Professors' dwellings are scattered over the east side along Madison Avenue. In the lower right are the Madison M. E. Church, Grace Episcopal Church with its rectory, and a row of small dwellings, and the Madison Academy stands near the lower left with houses around the Academy Road loop. A printed note beside the library records that no watchman is kept and that the buildings have steam heat and electric light. Blocks 53 and 54 are numbered, and a compass rose is drawn at the upper left.
notes: Georeferenced from two points only (Lancaster Road / Madison Avenue and a hand-picked Green Village Road / Vinton Road); low confidence.
Kings Road / Madison Avenue / Main Street lies about 8 percent beyond the drawn distance and was left out.
The modern Academy Road and Campus Drive lines do not follow the drawn loop and were not used.
100 ft. Drew Theological Seminary, Madison Av, Lancaster Rd, Green Village Rd, Academy Rd, Vinton Rd; two-point helmert.

sheet-23-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 23 is the upper two thirds of the sheet, drawn at 200 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left, unlike most sheets of the atlas. It covers the northwestern corner of the borough towards Convent Station: Madison Avenue crosses the part from Kitchell Avenue at the left to Morris Place at the right, Treadwell Avenue runs south from Madison Avenue, and Danforth Road and Fairwood Road appear at the upper right. The Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad runs along the top edge. The land is divided into large estates and their names are printed across them: the estate of H. McK. Twombly north of Madison Avenue, R. H. Williams, R. Parthenia V. Ross, the estate of Chas. M. Decker, and south of the avenue Enos Wilder Jr., Ada B. Olney, Mrs. R. F. Ballantine and L. L. Dunham. T. Jones, florist, has greenhouses on Kitchell Avenue. Buildings are few and widely spaced: dwellings, stables, garages, a gate house and a buried gasoline tank. The borough line runs along the south and west of the part, with Morris Township and Passaic Township named beyond it. The heavy line at the bottom separates this part from part 2, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, and the area south of Madison Avenue east of a pink line belongs to sheet 21.
notes: Kitchell Avenue is Kitchell Road today.
Estate of H. McK. Twombly north of Madison Avenue.
Drawn at 200 ft to an inch; the lower parts of the sheet are at 100 ft.

Three parts. Part 1: 200 ft, Madison Av from Kitchell Av to Morris Pl (Convent Station side, estates), north about -36 deg. Part 2: 100 ft, Woodland Rd, Loantara (Loantaka) Way, Gibbons Pl, Lathrop Av, Prospect Pl, Shunpike Rd. Part 3: 100 ft inset at the right of the lower half, Shunpike Rd between Loantaka Way and Prospect Pl, drawn at its own rotation.

sheet-23-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 23 is the lower part of the sheet, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, covering the southwestern corner of the borough on the Chatham Township line. Woodland Road runs along its top edge, under the heavy dividing line, and Loantara Way (Loantaka Way today) runs diagonally from Woodland Road down to Shunpike Road at the lower left. Gibbons Place runs south from Woodland Road on the right, with the short Lathrop Avenue leaving it to the east, and Prospect Place runs from Gibbons Place towards the lower left. Most of the part is the large undeveloped holding of F. H. Lovell, block 62, with one stuccoed dwelling near Woodland Road. Along Loantara Way and Gibbons Place there are a few dwellings and garages, the J. R. Mitchell property and smaller lots in block 73, and a row of houses on Prospect Place. The borough line runs along the left and bottom of the part with the Township of Chatham named beyond it, and block 72 lies west of Shunpike Road. Water pipes are drawn on Loantara Way, Gibbons Place and Prospect Place. The area right of the heavy vertical line is a separate inset (part 3), and the bottom right of the sheet carries the scale bar and the compass.
notes: Loantara Way is printed so; the street is Loantaka Way today.
F. H. Lovell holding fills most of block 62.

Three parts. Part 1: 200 ft, Madison Av from Kitchell Av to Morris Pl (Convent Station side, estates), north about -36 deg. Part 2: 100 ft, Woodland Rd, Loantara (Loantaka) Way, Gibbons Pl, Lathrop Av, Prospect Pl, Shunpike Rd. Part 3: 100 ft inset at the right of the lower half, Shunpike Rd between Loantaka Way and Prospect Pl, drawn at its own rotation.

sheet-23-3.description: Part 3 of sheet 23 is a small inset at the right of the lower half of the sheet, boxed off by heavy lines and drawn at 100 feet to an inch at a different rotation from part 2. It shows the western end of the area where Loantara Way, Prospect Place and Shunpike Road meet, south of Woodland Road on the Chatham Township line. Shunpike Road runs down the left side of the inset with the borough line along it, Loantara Way leaves it at the top towards the upper right, and Prospect Place crosses the lower part towards the right. Between Loantara Way and Prospect Place lies block 73 with a stuccoed dwelling of hollow tile and two other dwellings; block 72 lies west of Shunpike Road and block 75 south of Prospect Place. The street widths of Shunpike Road and Prospect Place (50 feet) are noted. The inset continues the area of part 2 beyond the bottom of the main drawing, so it overlaps part 2 on the ground near the Loantaka Way and Shunpike Road junction.
notes: Inset drawn at its own rotation; placed from two junctions only.

Three parts. Part 1: 200 ft, Madison Av from Kitchell Av to Morris Pl (Convent Station side, estates), north about -36 deg. Part 2: 100 ft, Woodland Rd, Loantara (Loantaka) Way, Gibbons Pl, Lathrop Av, Prospect Pl, Shunpike Rd.
